newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank keeps interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank keeps interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that its policy-making council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged at its regular meeting.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at three percent for the next two weeks.
The Bundesbank said it would set its next two repo tenders at a fixed rate of 3.00 percent, the rate that has prevailed since late August.
Economists had expected no change, arguing that the steady improvement in the German economy gave the central bank no reason to provide additional stimulation.

All 10 economists polled by Reuters who closely follow the Bundesbank said they expected the German central bank to keep rates on hold at the regular council meeting and indeed for the rest of the year.

The wide-spread consensus on rates comes at a time when Bundesbank council members have sent at times mixed signals about the future of interest rates, some saying they would consider supporting a rate cut if the economy slowed.
